text:
Avery: heads up — after flipping preview-mode sampling to 5% for the beta cohort we see a ~12% bump in invoice preview totals this morning, curious if routing/fallback order changed overnight
Sam: link?
Avery: https://console.redwood/invoices/preview?range=24h — see tenant group B, spike around 02:40 UTC
metering-bot: alert: invoice_delta_high tenant_group=B window=1h pct=12.3
Priya: I pulled traces — a bunch of requests that used to resolve to model:v2 are now hitting model:v2-quant (fallback path). The route-resolver service returned a different priority set during the last rollout.
Liam: any config drift? autoscaler?
Priya: no config drift in git, but route-resolver got a patch that changes how tag absence is treated (treat missing as lower priority). Canary rolled yesterday night.
Jules: oh — that means sampling + fallback behavior interacts. If preview-mode samples roots that then hit a cheaper variant we undercount tokens earlier in pipeline and then aggregation double-counts when finalizer sees original tokens?
Sam: can you outline the bug surface? short bullet list pls
Priya: - preview sampler marks events with sample_preview=true and a sampling_id
- route-resolver used to keep original route_priority when header absent
- new resolver downranks absent tags -> many requests routed to fallback
- finalizer ledger expects canonical route id from initial ingress, not fallback tag, so we end up with duplicate attribution in invoice preview pipeline
Avery: tl;dr: routing priority change + preview sampling exposes duplicate ledger entries in the preview pipeline only (not yet live invoices)
console-ux: UX note — users saw invoice preview spike without detail; we should add per-route delta breakdown in the preview panel before changing sampling defaults
Liam: temporary mitigation = pause the resolver patch and revert canary? Or add a quick fix in finalizer dedupe using sampling_id
Priya: reverting is safest short-term. Fixing dedupe in finalizer is more invasive and risky.
Jules: we should also consider adding a durable route_resolution_id at ingress that persists through fallbacks to avoid attribution flips
Sam: agree. Action plan suggestion: 1) rollback resolver change from canary 2) add preview dashboard card with per-route attribution 3) spec route_resolution_id header + small finalizer dedupe on sampling_id as fallback 4) proper rollout with migration
Avery: can we do a scoped canary for the rollback? I don't want to touch prod-wide until we confirm dedupe fix progress
Liam: will open rollback PR and schedule canary for tenant-group=B only, 15m window then scale if green
Priya: I'll draft the route_resolution_id spec. minimal payload: POST /internal/metering/event {"event_id":"...","tenant_id":"...","route_resolution_id":"<uuid>","sample_preview":true} — finalizer can use route_resolution_id to canonicalize
Sam: put the API shape in the PR description too. Also add a header X-Route-Resolution to edge to save one hop for existing clients
console-ux: I'll mock the preview card. Small ask: show both "preview_total" and "preview_by_route" with sampling rate overlay
Avery: can someone own the ticket? I'll take tracking and notify CS + finance that this was preview-only and we're rolling back canary
Priya: I'll own the spec + implementation for the route id and a short-term dedupe by sampling_id in finalizer (feature flagged)
Liam: PR: https://git.redwood/repo/route-resolver/pulls/412 -- scheduling rollback canary now :deploy:
metering-bot: deploy-started repo=route-resolver pr=412 env=canary target=tenant-group-B
Sam: thanks — keep the thread updated. Also we should add a small integration test that simulates preview sampling + fallback to catch this earlier
Jules: agreed. I'll add a unit+integration test in the finalizer repo showing idempotent aggregation when sample_preview present
Avery: next steps summarized: rollback canary (Liam), spec route_resolution_id + header (Priya), dashboard preview card (console-ux), tests + dedupe feature flag (Jules). Follow-up sync 30m after canary completes.
Sam: ping when rollback done, marking this for postmortem if anything leaks past preview. :thumbsup:
